body:
## What happens

The one line naming the skills a turn used is drawn while the turn runs and is
gone the moment it settles. Expanding the work chip does not bring it back.

So the question a person actually asks, "did it use my skill?", has no answer on
the surface. They ask it after the answer arrives, not during, and by then the
line has been folded away.

## Why

The row is written by `feed.note` (`internal/tui3/feed.go`), which leaves
`entry.told` false. `deriveWorkfolds` (`internal/tui3/workfold.go`) picks the
contiguous run between a question and its answer and covers it with the chip;
a plain note inside that run is covered with everything else. The open fold
draws its own caption and step rows and skips the entries underneath
(`internal/tui3/render.go`), so `ctrl+e` cannot reach it either.

`entry.told` is the existing exemption and it is the wrong one here: a told note
sets `blocked` in `deriveWorkfolds`, and `blocked` suppresses the chip for the
WHOLE group. Using it would mean every turn that used a skill keeps its raw
machinery on screen forever. That was tried and reverted.

## Replication

```go
// internal/tui3
f := &feed{live: -1, think: -1}
f.ingest(session.Event{Kind: session.EventUser, Text: "write the notes"})
f.ingest(session.Event{Kind: session.EventNotice, Text: "skills carried: release-notes",
    Skills: []string{"release-notes"}})
f.ingest(session.Event{Kind: session.EventTool, Name: "read"})
f.ingest(session.Event{Kind: session.EventAssistant, Text: "done", Settled: true})

folds := deriveWorkfolds(f.entries, 0)
// the skills entry's index falls inside [fold.start, fold.answer), so the chip covers it
```

## Acceptance

End to end first, through the real surface.

`internal/e2e`, after the answer has settled and the chip has closed, the frame
still carries `skills · ` followed by the skill's own name. Today the same frame
taken five seconds after Enter has it and the frame after the answer does not,
which is the whole bug.

Then a unit test in `internal/tui3` asserting the row is outside every fold's
covered range, whichever way it is kept.

## Two ways to fix it, neither chosen

1. A per-row keep that is not `blocked`. `phaseKeeps` is that list for phase
   folds; workfolds have no equivalent, and adding one means the fold's covered
   range stops being contiguous.
2. Carry the fact on the answer rather than in a notice, so it is drawn by the
   block that survives. That is the smaller surface change and the larger engine
   one, because `Event.Skills` today rides the notice at the START of the turn.

Option 2 also answers the question for a conversation reopened tomorrow, which
option 1 does not.
